segments.he: צָרִיךְ לְהִזָּהֵר שֶׁלּא לָבוֹא מִלֵּב נִשְׁבָּר לְעַצְבוּת
segments.en: When a person sees within himself that he has been lying in darkness for a long time and each time wishes to strive to find counsel to emerge from the darkness into the light, yet his hope is disappointed and he has not yet returned from the darkness in which he is caught — until it seems to him that he has no counsel at all, how to emerge from what he needs to emerge from, and his counsel is very confused — then this itself is his remedy: to cry out about this very thing to Hashem, that he has fallen so low that he does not know the complete counsel, how to emerge from darkness into light. For certainly there is no despair in the world at all, and certainly even in his place there is counsel for how to emerge from darkness to light, from bad to good — only that through his sins the counsel has been hidden from him, in the aspect of: "who is this that darkens counsel with words" [Iyov 38:2]. And therefore his remedy is that he should know at least the truth — that he has fallen so low and distanced himself so far that he knows no counsel at all — and he should cry out about this very matter to Hashem to teach him the counsel and the way how to conduct himself in truth. As King Dovid cried out greatly about this: "How long shall I take counsel in my soul" [Tehillim 13:3]. For one who wishes to enter the service of Hashem in truth must pray very greatly to Hashem to merit complete and true counsel, so that he merits to return in truth. For in every place he is, there is certainly counsel there for how to emerge from there — only one must pray greatly to Hashem to merit knowing the complete counsel.

segments.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה צָרִיךְ לִצְעק וְלִבְכּוֹת הַרְבֵּה לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְשַׁבֵּר לִבּוֹ מְאד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב לֵב נִשְׁבָּר וְנִדְכֶּה אֱלקִים לא תִבְזֶה אֲבָל אַף עַל פִּי כֵן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בָּקִי בַּהֲלָכָה שֶׁלּא יִתְרַחֵק חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹתֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה. כִּי בְּכָל דַּרְכֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה יֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּחִינַת צַדִּיקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם וְהַהֵפֶךְ בְּחִינַת פּוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם.
segments.en: When the great darkness intensifies upon an upright person who wishes to draw close to Hashem — especially at the time of prayer — and the darkness surrounds him from every side and from all directions: this is the aspect of Esther's entry into the house of the wicked Achashverosh, a house full of idols and impurities — which is the aspect of the very intensification of the darkness, when one knows no way, counsel, or stratagem to be saved from it. And then the essential counsel is only truth — to speak the word in truth and to cry out to Hashem in truth. This is the aspect of what Esther cried when she entered a house full of idols: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" [Tehillim 22:2]. And through this the light of truth shone upon her — drawn from the aspect of Mordechai, who is the Tzaddik of the generation, the very essence of truth. And this guards every single person in Yisrael: when one cries out to Hashem in truth, even if one has fallen to wherever one has fallen, Heaven forbid — even if darkness surrounds one from every side — even so, when one believes in Hashem in truth in simplicity, believing in the one G-d, and cries out to Him in truth: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" and entreats Him in truth — then the truth shines upon him and he sees the openings and emerges from darkness to light. And then not only can the Sitra Achra and the darkness not prevent or confuse his prayer — but he also merits to open a path for others as well, to bring others out of the darkness and return them to teshuvah. As written there [Likutay Moharan 112] on the verse: "and the door of the ark you shall place at its side" — see there.

segments.he: בְּחִינַת זָכָה נַעֲשֶׂה לוֹ סַם חַיִּים לא זָכָה וְכוּ'. כִּי בְּוַדַּאי צָרִיךְ הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה לִסְבּל בִּזְיוֹנוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים בְּכַמָּה בְּחִינוֹת וְכַמְבאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ"ל. שֶׁעִקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁמַע בִּזְיוֹנוֹ יִדּם וְיִשְׁתּק וִיקַיֵּם דּוֹם לַה' וְכוּ' וּבִכְלַל זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ לִסְבּל בִּזְיוֹנוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים מֵעַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִינַת חֶרְפָּה שָׁבְרָה לִבִּי וְכוּ' כִּי צָרִיךְ לְהִתְבַּיֵּשׁ בְּעַצְמוֹ מֵעֲוֹנוֹתָיו וּפְגָמָיו עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁפָּךְ דָּמָיו בְּקִרְבּוֹ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כָּל הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵרָה וּמִתְבַּיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו. אֲבָל אַף עַל פִּי כֵן צְרִיכִין לִהְיוֹת בָּקִי בַּהֲלָכָה זאת מְאד שֶׁלּא יָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְעַצְבוּת וּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִזְהִיר אֲדוֹנֵנוּ מוֹרֵנוּ וְרַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל זֶה וְאָמַר שֶׁלֵּב נִשְׁבָּר הוּא עִנְיָן אַחֵר מֵעַצְבוּת. וּצְרִיכִין לִזָּהֵר שֶׁלּא יִתְאַחֵז הָעַצְבוּת מֵהַלֵּב נִשְׁבָּר עַל כֵּן הִזְהִיר לְהִתְגַּבֵּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל הַיּוֹם בְּשִׂמְחָה בְּכָל דַּרְכֵי עֲצוֹתָיו הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת. רַק בְּשָׁעָה מְיֻחֶדֶת יִהְיֶה לוֹ לֵב נִשְׁבָּר לְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּבֵן לִפְנֵי אָבִיו וְכוּ' וְכָל זֶה כָּלוּל בִּבְחִינַת בָּקִי בַּהֲלָכָה הַנַּ"ל. (הִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת הֲלָכָה ז אוֹת מה):
segments.en: One who wishes to conduct commerce and earn money and wealth must be very careful to reckon his ways and judge himself at all times and examine his deeds at every moment. For through the mishpat [self-judgment] described above, specifically, one can conduct commerce in holiness so that it succeeds — for one who does business is in the aspect of bringing souls close to Hashem, for there are very high holy sparks in commerce that need to be refined through business dealings, as Rabbainu of blessed memory explained many times. And therefore one engaged in commerce must guard himself greatly lest the evil of those souls and sparks he is refining through his business take hold of him. But in truth commerce is a very great thing — only one must guard oneself as above. Therefore he needs the mishpat described — to judge himself personally on all matters he does, whether it is thus fitting for him to act and spend his days in such deeds. And through this mishpat he arouses the heart's fervor, which is the aspect of fire — and through this fire he burns away the evil so it does not take hold of him, and so it does not take hold of those sparks and souls he is engaged in refining through commerce.
